title: We Can’t Stop Staring at the NSX-Based JAS Tensei

body_markdown:
Acura is busily plotting the third-generation NSX, which will reportedly make its debut by the end of the decade with electric power. In the meantime, an Italian company named JAS Motorsport has[teamed up with Pininfarina](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/honda-nsx-gets-restomod-treatment-from-pininfarina/) to put a modern twist on[the original model](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/2003-honda-nsx-r-tops-1m-and-breaks-record-at-villa-deste/) . Unveiled at the Paris auto show, the JAS Tensei is a restomodded NSX with a carbon fiber body and V-6 power.


The restomod treatment is relatively subtle at first glance, but JAS explains that Pininfarina tweaked every single visual detail to bring the NSX into the modern era. This partially explains the name: Tensei translates to “rebirth” or “reincarnation” in Japanese.


Built with carbon fiber, the Tensei is wider and lower than the original NSX. It certainly looks newer thanks to styling cues such as pop-up headlights with LED elements, new-look rear lights, and a set of 19-inch front and 20-inch rear center-locking wheels, but several key details remain untouched. Pininfarina notably retained the side-mounted air intakes and the wrap-around rear window.

The emphasis put on ergonomics helped the first-gen NSX stand out from its rivals. JAS kept the cabin’s basic layout while adding 21st-century tech, such as a digital instrument cluster, a touchscreen-based infotainment system, and new switches. The tech isn’t in-your-face or excessive, at least not at first glance, and the cabin remains characterized by a driver-focused approach to design.


Power comes from an evolution of the original NSX’s naturally-aspirated V-6. Designed by a British company named Judd Power, the engine features 3.5 liters of displacement, a billet crankshaft, forged connecting rods, and forged pistons, among other weight-saving components. JAS quotes an output of about 420 horsepower. For context, the most powerful version of the first-generation NSX used a 3.2-liter version of the V-6 rated at 290 horsepower. The six-cylinder is linked to a six-speed manual transmission.


JAS completely re-engineered the suspension with KW coilovers on both axles, a front-axle lift system, and specific roll bars. The electro-hydraulic steering rack was developed specifically for the Tensei, while Brembo brakes keep the V-6’s power in check.


The JAS Tensei will be built “in an ultra-limited series,” according to the manufacturer, though a specific number hasn’t been released. Pricing isn’t available, either, but we wouldn’t be surprised if the born-again NSX lands with a seven-digit price tag. The model will be built by JAS near Milan, Italy, and buyers will be able to work directly with Pininfarina to customize their car.
